bug_semantics: Webmin miniserv.pl authenticates SSL-client-certificate users by mapping a certificate DN through find_user_by_cert() and setting $validated=2. After trust_real_ip was reused as a proxy-header trust flag, a client-supplied X-SSL-Client-DN header was treated as that DN without a verified TLS client certificate from this connection. With proxy-IP trust enabled and at least one user bound to a client cert, an unauthenticated peer that reaches miniserv directly (not via the intended reverse proxy) can forge X-SSL-Client-DN and impersonate that user (CWE-290). Preconditions match the vendor write-up: trust_real_ip plus client-cert users; AC:H/AT:P in the CVSS vectors.
flaw_origin: The header-to-identity mapping was first written in b3b5fff0dc48574d71db12cdfd538c9fd11a55e3 (2023-07-28) while implementing GitHub issue #1962 (client certs behind a reverse proxy). That commit added miniserv.pl lines that call find_user_by_cert($header{'x-ssl-client-dn'}) whenever trust_real_ip is set, gated only by that existing proxy-IP flag rather than a trusted-proxy allowlist or a verified TLS peer. 4197e6177291f60411636f08ef1c8fc2106bf577 then lifted the surrounding $use_ssl && $verified_client guard so the same header authenticates with no client cert at all, which is the unauthenticated path described by CISA/GHSA.

Vendor page https://webmin.com/security/#webmin-prior-to-2202 assigns CVE-2026-56020 to 'SSL certificates from clients may be trusted unexpectedly' and credits Keigo YAMAZAKI (LAC Co., Ltd.).

Vendor mechanism: if Webmin trusts proxy-provided remote IPs and users authenticate with client SSL certs, a browser connecting directly can send a forged header to fake the client certificate. Vendor affected range is 2.202 and below; recommended upgrade is 2.301 or later plus disabling Trust level for proxy headers when direct client access is possible.

CISA CSAF VA-26-169-02 / CVE JSON describe miniserv.pl forged-header DN spoofing and currently say 'Fixed in 2.202' / affected <2.202. That patched boundary is inconsistent with git: tag 2.202 (25321b467b2945d14de06781f10a98ca381a1e23, 2024-08-11) still contains the unauthenticated X-SSL-Client-DN path at miniserv.pl:1704-1715. GHSA/NVD originally said fixed in 2.641, mixing this CVE with the later trusted_proxies work and with CVE-2026-56022 (2.640 2FA bypass).

BIC search: git log -S 'x-ssl-client-dn' -- miniserv.pl first introduces the auth use in b3b5fff0dc48574d71db12cdfd538c9fd11a55e3 ('If trusting the remote IP, also trust the proxied SSL client cert', issue #1962). git log -L 1693,1702:miniserv.pl at that commit confirms those four lines are the first write; earlier history only mapped Net::SSLeay peer cert DNs via find_user_by_cert.

Vulnerable lines at BIC miniserv.pl:1696-1698: if ($config{'trust_real_ip'} && !$u && $header{'x-ssl-client-dn'}) { # Use proxied client cert; $u = &find_user_by_cert($header{'x-ssl-client-dn'}); } then $authuser=$u; $validated=2. trust_real_ip itself was older (2969f2f20) and only used for X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP.

Expansion 4197e6177291f60411636f08ef1c8fc2106bf577 (2023-08-11, first in tag 2.102) changed the outer guard to ($use_ssl && $verified_client || $config{'trust_real_ip'} && $header{'x-ssl-client-dn'}), enabling the unauthenticated/non-SSL header login. That is not the first write of the flawed mapping, so it is not the BIC.

Later hardening, not the BIC and not the first fix: ba336c297b30e61511f02ea9eff3e86c517a9ec3 (2026-04-14, in 2.640+) requires X-SSL-Client-Verify =~ /^success/; 241abfe71951e27b301b134ca5a954ba6f40d12e (Joe Cooper, 2026-05-10, first tag 2.641) drops X-SSL-Client-* when trusted_proxies is non-empty and the TCP peer is not on the list (CHANGELOG 2.641 'Added support for trusted proxy IP addresses'). Empty trusted_proxies still honors the header. 463fcea7306873ae6f53929584f5646823fb8608 (2026-06-30, branch remotes/origin/dev/req-trusted-proxy only, not an ancestor of HEAD/2.660) would require an explicit trusted proxy before honoring cert headers; it is unreleased.
